item.title: ITP Awareness Week - LightUp4ITP
item.description:
Tuesday, 22 September 2026

City Hall will be lit Purple to support ITP Awareness Week - LightUp4ITP

Global ITP Awareness Week (21 to 27 September 2026), is dedicated to raising public awareness of the rare autoimmune blood disorder Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP) and to highlighting the ITP patient experience. ITP is a rare autoimmune disorder in which the body’s immune system attacks healthy platelets and/or suppresses platelet production, resulting in low platelet counts. Platelets help the blood clot, and individuals with ITP typically have a low platelet count. It affects children and adults. There is no cure. For most people, there is no known cause. ITP Australia and New Zealand's mission is to provide up-to-date information, education, support and advocacy for ITP patients and the ITP community. itpaustralia.org.au

This Light Up is organised by: ITP Australia Ltd

item.title: Dementia Action Week
item.description:
Wednesday, 23 September 2026

Story Bridge will be lit Blue to support Dementia Action Week

Dementia is Australia's leading cause of death, but it's not talked about nearly enough. This Dementia Action Week, we're asking every Australian to help change that, one conversation at a time. An estimated 446,500 Australians live with dementia, and 1.7 million people are involved in their care. A national conversation about dementia is made up of thousands of smaller ones - in GP clinics, workplaces, community halls and family homes.?Every conversation can tell someone it’s safe to speak up, that they’re not alone, and connects them to support they didn't know exists.

This Light Up is organised by: Dementia Australia

item.title: Childhood Cancer Awareness Month
item.description:
Sunday, 27 September 2026

Reddacliff Place sculptures will be lit Gold to support Childhood Cancer Awareness Month

September is Childhood Cancer Awareness Month.
The initiative aims to raise awareness of childhood cancer and unite the community in support of children undergoing treatment, survivors, bereaved families and healthcare professionals. Gold is the internationally recognised colour for childhood cancer awareness and symbolises hope, courage and solidarity. This year's request is inspired by the experiences of Queensland families, including those who relocate to Brisbane for treatment, and the illumination of these landmarks will provide a visible show of support, honour children lost to cancer, highlight the importance of continued investment in childhood cancer research and ensure that no child or family facing childhood cancer feels alone.

This Light Up is organised by: Kid's Cancer Project

item.description:
Saturday, 3 October 2026

City Hall will be lit Black, Red and Yellow to celebrate German National Day
 
German National Day, celebrated on 3 October each year, symbolises the reunification of Germany in 1990 and honours the values of peace, democracy and solidarity that emerged from this historic moment. item.title: EMMM Day
item.description:
Monday, 12 October 2026

Kangaroo Point Bridge will be lit Red to support EMMM Day

EMMM Day raises awareness of the harm experienced by children and young people when safe and meaningful family relationships are damaged, restricted, or severed through coercive post-separation family dynamics.
The day supports public education about psychological and relational pressures that can affect children, including repeated negative messaging, distorted information, fear-based claims, loyalty demands, and emotional expectations that interfere with a child's identity, attachment, development, and family connections.
It recognises the impact on children, displaced parents, grandparents, siblings, and extended family members, including ambiguous loss and disenfranchised grief, while making clear that genuine safety concerns, family violence, abuse, and neglect must be carefully assessed and never minimised. Its purpose is to promote early recognition, child protection, critical thinking, and safe, healthy family relationships wherever appropriate.

This Light Up is organised by: Eeny Meeny Miney Mo Foundation Ltd

item.title: Anti-Poverty Week
item.description:
Saturday, 17 October 2026

Victoria Bridge will be lit Blue and Green to support Anti-Poverty Week

Anti-Poverty Week supports the Australian community to have an increased understanding of poverty and to take action collectively to end it. Since 2002, we’ve been active every year in the week around the 17th of October, the United Nations Day for the Eradication of Poverty. During this week, we encourage all Australians to take action and focus on positive solutions to end poverty. We work with our network of diverse voices and organisations in order to increase awareness of poverty in Australia. We reach out to audiences who are not already at the forefront of this work including younger Australians and Federal politicians. Each year we choose an evidence-based solution to be a focus and partner with the leading campaign/organisation in that space to take action to end poverty.

This Light Up is organised by: Micah Projects

Anti-Poverty Week supports the Australian community to have an increased understanding of poverty and to take action collectively to end it. Since 2002, we’ve been active every year in the week around the 17th of October, the United Nations Day for the Eradication of Poverty. During this week, we encourage all Australians to take action and focus on positive solutions to end poverty. We work with our network of diverse voices and organisations in order to increase awareness of poverty in Australia. We reach out to audiences who are not already at the forefront of this work including younger Australians and Federal politicians. Each year we choose an evidence-based solution to be a focus and partner with the leading campaign/organisation in that space to take action to end poverty.
This Light Up is organised by: Micah Projects

item.title: Light It Red for Dyslexia Awareness
item.description:
Sunday, 18 October 2026

Victoria Bridge will be lit Red to support Light It Red for Dyslexia Awareness

Light it Red for Dyslexia Awareness is a volunteer initiative by Code REaD Dyslexia Network, a national registered charity, to light significant monuments, buildings and landmarks across
Australia in RED for Dyslexia Awareness. Approximately 10-20% of Australians have dyslexia, making it one of the country's most common learning differences. Despite this, many people continue to face barriers to early identification, appropriate support and equal opportunities. Through Light it Red, we aim to increase understanding, challenge misconceptions and inspire positive change.

This Light Up is organised by: Code REaD Dyslexia Network
